selected.item: Apple ML Research released FastFrames, a family of autoregressive two-step video diffusion models for interactive-latency 480p video generation, on November 16, 2026 (weights on Hugging Face; code public November 17). FastFrames-S (1.3B) generates 832x480 video, 81 frames at 16 fps, at about 36 ms per frame on a single B200-class GPU; FastFrames-L (14B) runs at about 45 ms per frame on eight GPUs. Both are two-step models: FastFrames-S keeps a two-step frame-wise Causal Forcing++ generator frozen and trains the surrounding networks, while FastFrames-L distills Wan2.1-T2V-14B into a two-step causal model. An optimized LingBot 1.3B with 16x speedup for fluid camera-conditioned control is also released. Checkpoints are under the Apple Research Model License (research only); code is under the Apple Sample Code License.
selected.note: The Hugging Face model card itself carries no date line, so the November 16 weights date is recorded from the card creation date as reported by multiple independent secondary sources (TSN, The Reel Stack), with code going public November 17. The arXiv paper is arXiv:2611.23226. Latency figures are the authors' own measurements on B200-class hardware. The release is research-only, not a product feature.

selected.item: Kyutai released AURA (AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar) on November 20, 2026, per its official blog dated 2026-11-20 (paper arXiv:2611.26540 dated November 19). AURA is a family of causal, few-step speech-to-video models that stream talking-head video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, needing only the current chunk's audio to start. AURA 1.3B streams 576p video at 20.7 fps end-to-end on a single H100 for 16 Hz playback (23x faster than its bidirectional teacher) and AURA 5B streams 720p at 9.7 fps (17x faster than its teacher). Both are 4-step causal students distilled from 50-step bidirectional teachers. Weights, inference code, a dataset of 30,000 synthetic videos with precomputed teacher trajectories, and a live demo are released. AURA 1.3B is under CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); AURA 5B is under Snap Inc.'s non-commercial license.
selected.note: The November 20 date is the Kyutai official blog date; the arXiv paper is dated November 19. Performance figures are Kyutai's own measurements on a single H100 GPU. Both weights are non-commercial only.

selected.item: AMD announced Nitro-P on November 20, 2026, on its official ROCm blog. Nitro-P is an end-to-end pixel-space text-to-image diffusion framework that removes the VAE decoder from the inference pipeline: a patch-level E-MMDiT semantic modeling component is joined hierarchically to a lightweight U-Net pixel-reconstruction decoder with modulation-guided semantic injection. The main network has 679M parameters and uses Qwen3-1.7B as the text encoder. AMD reports a GenEval score of 0.88 at 512x512 (0.87 at 1024x1024) and throughput of 10.26 samples/s on a single AMD Instinct MI300X GPU at 512px with batch size 32; the distilled one-step variant reaches 90.02 samples/s. Model weights and complete training code are released. Training used 25M publicly available images.
selected.note: The ROCm blog page itself carries no date line in the fetched text, so the November 20 announcement date is recorded from the announcement coverage (AI Weekly, TLDR, hane-lab) that cites the ROCm blog. The Hugging Face model page amd/Nitro-P is linked from the blog's Additional Resources. No license is set on the model page, so no license is asserted here. Performance figures are AMD's own reported numbers.
